_readme: Copy to config/profile.json and edit. Everything the agent knows about you lives here; no code changes needed. Run 'python run.py profile-from-resume resume.txt' to have Claude draft this from your resume, or start from a ready-made profile in config/profiles/.
name: Your Name
headline: Short description of the roles you want
home_base: City, ST (metro you can commute into)
resume_summary: 3-6 sentences: current role and scope, what you own, the size of team or business, prior roles, education, tools. Written in third person. This is the single most important field. The model reads it to judge fit, so specifics beat adjectives.
_titles: Tier 1 = the job you want. Tier 2 = adjacent, worth seeing. Matching is word-boundary aware and case-insensitive; substrings of a title match, so 'content director' hits 'Content Director, Brand'.
_blocks: Hard rejects. A title hit here never reaches your inbox and never appears in the ranked tail. Use for functions that share your vocabulary but are not your job.
_seniority: Title words that signal level. Lead scores higher than senior.
_locations: allow = places you would work. block = places you would not. Neither is a hard reject: a blocked location is a heavy penalty, so the role still appears at the bottom with the reason shown.
_keywords: Vocabulary from postings you would want. strong = the language of your actual job. good = supporting context. Scored from the posting body, capped so a keyword-stuffed listing cannot dominate.
_llm: Plain-language bullets handed to Claude for the judgment pass. Write these the way you would brief a recruiter.
fit_signals: Leads or mentors a team, or owns a function end to end
Sits in the org where this work actually reports
anti_signals: Junior individual contributor or coordinator level
_skip: Companies you never want to see. Patterns catch staffing and recruiting firms, which repost the same roles endlessly and are the single largest noise source in most searches.
_thresholds: strong and look set the two top sections. llm_floor is the score a posting needs before it costs an API call. Raise strong for a quieter inbox, lower look for a longer middle section.
